- Keep responses concise, structured, and actionable and avoid long paragraphs.
- Prefer small, focused changes that follow existing project conventions.
- Avoid unnecessary rewrites, duplication, assumptions, and unrelated fixes.
- Reuse existing components, utilities, patterns, and documentation where appropriate.
- Make functionality modular when it improves maintainability.
- Validate changes with the narrowest relevant check available.
- Ask for clarification only when ambiguity would materially affect the implementation.
- Explain assumptions and mention remaining risks or unverified checks.
